title: Doctor Ronnie Will See You Now
description: Ronnie decides hosting a radio show is basically a medical degree and opens the phones for a health advice hour. Real worries, confident wrong answers, and one cure for everything: sweat it out.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight, the lines are open for our first ever Health Advice Hour. You got an ache? A pain? A worry? <p:0.3> Doctor Ronnie will see you now.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, you are not a doctor.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Twenty years on the air, Barry. That's basically a residency. <p:0.3> Mildred, you're on the line.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, hello dear. I've had this sore throat and a little fever for, oh, going on a week now, and it just won't quit. And at my age I do worry. Should I be concerned?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred, relax. That's nothing. That's a classic sweat-it-out situation.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A what?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Here's what you do, sweetheart. Go sit in your car. Windows up, heater on full blast. <p:0.3> You let that fever cook itself right out of you.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Ohh. My mother used to say sweating breaks a fever, so that does make a kind of sense.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It does not make sense. Mildred, maybe just see a real doc...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Next caller! Steve, talk to me.

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Yeah, hi, so I've been getting these sharp pains in my chest when I go up the stairs, and there's like a tingling going down my left arm. Honestly it's got me pretty scared.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Steve, Steve, Steve. I know exactly what that is. You skip breakfast, don't you?

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: I... I mean, sometimes?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Same as me! It's an empty-chest situation. You need to LINE that chest. Big greasy sandwich. <p:0.3> And folks, Big Mike's Subs, that's where I line mine.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, chest pain and a left arm? That sounds like it could be his heart...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: His heart's fine, Barry, it's homesick for a hoagie. And Steve, if the sandwich doesn't do it? <p:0.3> Sweat it out.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Hi, yes, so I've got this mole on my shoulder and it's, well, it's changed shape lately, and the color's gone all uneven, and I'm wondering if I ought to get it looked at by someone.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Patricia, congratulations! You know what that is? <p:0.3> That's a free beauty mark.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: A... beauty mark? But it wasn't there before, and it's been getting darker.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Dab a little concealer on it, forget it ever happened. And if you want it lighter? <p:0.3> Sauna. Sweat that color right out of it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You cannot sweat out a changing mole, Ronnie, that's the one thing everyone knows to get checked...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Darnell! You're up. What's ailing you, friend?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: So I passed out at work yesterday, just dropped, and now the doctor wants to run a bunch of tests on my blood sugar. But that's a lot of money. Is it even worth it?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Tests are a scam, Darnell. Fainting is just the body doing a little free reboot. Healthy, even.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A reboot.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You power through it. Energy drink, stand up faster next time. <p:0.3> Me? I have never once been to a doctor, Darnell, and look at me. Picture of health.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: I can't actually see you, though. It's radio.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Trust me. Radiant. And after the energy drink, Darnell? <p:0.3> You sweat it out.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's always sweat it out. Every single one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Because it works, Barry! Last call. Frank, you're on with Doctor Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: I was outside last night. Ice that wasn't there before. <p:0.3> I went down hard — heard a loud crack — and there were pigeons watching, Ronnie. <p:0.3> My ankle's gone purple, swelled to twice the size. <p:0.3> This wasn't an accident.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Frank, can you still feel it?

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Oh, I can feel it. <p:0.3> They put it there for a reason, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then it's not broken! Broken means numb. <p:0.3> So here's the plan, Frank. Hot sauna, get that ankle in there, sweat the swelling right out.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. Ronnie, please.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And then, once it's nice and loose, you walk it off. Briskly! That sets the bone back straight.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I am BEGGING you to stop talking. Frank, go to a hospital. Right now. RIGHT now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Barry's a worrier, Frank. <p:0.3> Sweat it out. We'll be right back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: We got a voicemail in. It's from Mildred. <p:0.3> Our very first caller.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hello again, dears. I did sit in the hot car like the doctor said. <p:0.3> I got a parking ticket, and now my fever's much worse. But Ronnie was so confident, I just believed him!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's the malpractice, folks. <p:0.3> Right there.
